title: My partner and I fled for our lives after my laptop exploded - but this is why I ran back inside my home SIX times as it burned to the ground
text:
A heroic father met his burning home six times to rescue the beloved dogs of his partner, suffering burns in his torso and face, after a laptop caught fire.
Ben Sommerville and Caroline Ward lost all their possessions when their home in Calne, Wiltshire, exploded in flames on Sunday, February 9.
Sommerville, 39, bravely ran into the house in an attempt to save the three dogs of Mrs. Ward, La Tortuga and her kitten.
He managed to save the dogs: the three -year -old American bulldog Ruby, the French bulldog Cedric and the English bulldog Ethel, both seven.
Tragically Catspian, the kitten who gathered when they began to leave, lost their lives along with the Ward turtle, Brutus, whom he had for 13 years.
Only two nights before the devastating fire, the children of Mr. Sommerville,, 11, 12 and 15, had stayed with them at home. “We are very grateful that they weren’t there that night,” he told Mailonline.
Mr. Sommerville, who works as a little hand, had run to the house while using nothing more than a pair of jeans and suffered burns on the face, back and chest and said that most of his hair went, including his bun .
But he said that the community has recovered around the couple, taking care of their dogs generously while staying in a hotel.
And because Mr. Sommerville is very high, 7 feet with a size of 17 feet, he was worried about getting new clothes, but a local man who makes personalized hoodies refused to take the payment of him.

When telling the terrible night, he told Mailonline: ‘My partner and I was lying around 9 o’clock at an early night and a hug. Half an hour later, I heard our kitten make a whistle noise and thought that I had accidentally turned on the shower.
‘I went to take a look and the shower was off, but I thought I could smell smoke. I told my partner to wear some clothes just in case and lowered the stairs.
‘The smell was much stronger and I could see smoke coming out from under the door.
‘I ran the stairs, shouting to leave, leave now. The lights go out just when we were running out.
When they were safe, they called the Fire Brigade. The couple praised emergency services, saying they were in the house in 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, Mrs. Ward was ‘shouting for the dogs’, so her partner ran again.

He continued: ‘One was outside the back door. I continued my breathing and ran around the house and breathed again before trying to find them again.
‘I had the torch of my phone on, and I was talking on the phone with the firefighters who told me to come out now.
‘But if the dogs died, my Missus would be with emotional scars. I managed to find the two dogs and throw them outside.
‘I ran up stairs to try to find the cat, but I knew he had probably left. The smoke was so bad and thick that I couldn’t see much.
When the firefighters arrived, Mr. Sommerville was “hitting” his neighbor’s door to wake them up, knowing that they had a newborn baby.
“It was really scary,” he said. It was badly burned throughout the body. I used to have a bun of man but my hair was burned and my beard is really crunchy. Most of my hair is gone.
‘I didn’t realize until after that they burned me all my back and shoulders. The rain probably saved me from the worst of burns.

‘The next thing I remember was that I was in the hospital and they were applying burn ointment. I had burns on my face, all I had was a pair of jeans.
‘He was not afraid, just logic. My partner’s dogs were there.
Speaking about the cause of the fire, he said: ‘The only thing different from that night was that my partner had connected his laptop to load. It was renewed, we got it two years ago.
The father said he has been overwhelmed with the kindness of the community.
He said: ‘People have been phenomenal. I had no clothes and because I am 7 feet high with a size of 17 feet, it is difficult to find it in the stores. A guy who sells me with a personalized hood refused to take the payment of them.
‘We are in a hotel and folded the rules to keep the smallest dog with us: a friend has one and a neighbor is taking care of the other.
‘I didn’t realize that there would be a great community in the world. We were very lucky. He has approached us much more.

We are very grateful that they weren’t there that night. They loved Catspian. We gave them the news and they took it very well, they have really been understanding. ‘
He published a photo of the little kitten on Facebook, saying: “Rip, little friend, I will really miss you.”
He added sadly: ‘People have never called me a hero before, I would like it to see me more as one. I am so crispy, I see myself like a scarecrow.
It has been so overwhelming. It has been difficult to sleep when we go to bed.
‘There is a wooden fire in the hotel’s lobby, and when we smell the smoke that we panic for a second, thinking that it was happening again.
‘It was scary. The most important thing is that we have ourselves and we are together.
A spokesman for the fire and rescue service of Dorset and Wiltshire said: ‘In the arrival teams they found a fire on the ground floor of a private home on terraces and six firefighters in breathing devices used two hose reel jets, a jet main and mechanical ventilation extinguishing fire.
“Two victims were transmitted to the hospital by ambulance and our stop went at 10:45 pm.”
